description: Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly greater than 0.0005 are included.

c.request: For fee records that clear the 0.0005 maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) threshold, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, work out the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, as long as that overall mean isn't missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Show the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and the relative ratio for the top 10 orders by relative ratio, highest first, with missing values last. Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly greater than 0.0005 are included.
c.sql:
WITH filtered_fees AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    rebtotal,
    rebrate,
    feerate
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate > 0.0005
),
order_averages AS (
  SELECT
    orderslink,
    AVG(rebtotal) as avg_rebtotal,
    AVG(CASE WHEN rebrate IS NOT NULL AND feerate IS NOT NULL AND feerate != 0 THEN rebrate / feerate ELSE NULL END) as avg_ratio
  FROM filtered_fees
  WHERE orderslink IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall_mean_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as mean_ratio
  FROM order_averages
),
with_relative_ratio AS (
  SELECT
    oa.orderslink,
    oa.avg_rebtotal,
    oa.avg_ratio,
    CASE 
      WHEN om.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL AND oa.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
      THEN oa.avg_ratio / om.mean_ratio 
      ELSE NULL 
    END as relative_ratio
  FROM order_averages oa
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean_calc om
)
SELECT
  orderslink,
  avg_rebtotal,
  avg_ratio,
  relative_ratio
FROM with_relative_ratio
ORDER BY 
  relative_ratio IS NULL,
  relative_ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;

a.request: Using only fee records whose maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) is greater than 0.0005, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, compute the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, provided that overall mean is not missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Return the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and this relative ratio for the 10 orders with the highest relative ratio, sorted from highest to lowest with missing values last.
a.sql:
WITH filtered_fees AS (
  SELECT orderslink, rebtotal, rebrate, feerate
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate > 0.0005
),
per_order_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    AVG(rebtotal) as avg_rebtotal,
    AVG(rebrate / feerate) as avg_ratio
  FROM filtered_fees
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as mean_ratio
  FROM per_order_stats
),
with_relative_ratio AS (
  SELECT 
    pos.orderslink,
    pos.avg_rebtotal,
    pos.avg_ratio,
    CASE 
      WHEN om.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL 
      THEN pos.avg_ratio / om.mean_ratio 
      ELSE NULL 
    END as relative_ratio
  FROM per_order_stats pos
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
)
SELECT 
  orderslink,
  avg_rebtotal,
  avg_ratio,
  relative_ratio
FROM with_relative_ratio
ORDER BY 
  relative_ratio IS NULL,
  relative_ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;

b.request: Filter fee records to include only those where rebrate > 0.0005 (strictly greater); group by orderslink; for each order calculate average rebtotal and average (rebrate / feerate); compute the global mean of all per-order average ratios; divide each order's average ratio by this global mean; return the top 10 orders by relative ratio in descending order with nulls last, displaying orderslink, average rebtotal, average ratio, and relative ratio.
b.sql: WITH filtered_fees AS (SELECT orderslink, rebtotal, rebrate, feerate FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 AND feerate IS NOT NULL AND feerate != 0), order_stats AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) as avg_rebtotal, AVG(rebrate / feerate) as avg_ratio FROM filtered_fees GROUP BY orderslink), global_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as global_mean_ratio FROM order_stats) SELECT os.orderslink, os.avg_rebtotal, os.avg_ratio, CASE WHEN gm.global_mean_ratio IS NOT NULL AND gm.global_mean_ratio != 0 THEN os.avg_ratio / gm.global_mean_ratio ELSE NULL END as relative_ratio FROM order_stats os CROSS JOIN global_mean gm ORDER BY CASE WHEN relative_ratio IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, relative_ratio DESC LIMIT 10
b.raw: Filter fee records to include only those where rebrate > 0.0005 (strictly greater); group by orderslink; for each order calculate average rebtotal and average (rebrate / feerate); compute the global mean of all per-order average ratios; divide each order's average ratio by this global mean; return the top 10 orders by relative ratio in descending order with nulls last, displaying orderslink, average rebtotal, average ratio, and relative ratio.

d.request: Select fee records where rebrate > 0.0005, group by orderslink, calculate average rebtotal and average (rebrate/feerate) for each order, compute the overall mean of these per-order averages, divide each order's average ratio by the overall mean to get relative ratio, and output the top 10 orders by highest relative ratio (nulls last), displaying orderslink, average rebtotal, average ratio, and relative ratio.
d.sql:
WITH filtered_fees AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate > 0.0005
),
per_order_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    AVG(rebtotal) as avg_rebtotal,
    AVG(rebrate / feerate) as avg_ratio
  FROM filtered_fees
  WHERE feerate IS NOT NULL AND feerate != 0
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as overall_avg_ratio
  FROM per_order_stats
),
with_relative_ratio AS (
  SELECT 
    pos.orderslink,
    pos.avg_rebtotal,
    pos.avg_ratio,
    pos.avg_ratio / om.overall_avg_ratio as relative_ratio
  FROM per_order_stats pos
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
)
SELECT 
  orderslink,
  avg_rebtotal,
  avg_ratio,
  relative_ratio
FROM with_relative_ratio
ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10
